strengths: Root-cause diagnosis is correct and well-evidenced: the WIP comment in matmul_shared_coopmat.axc says 'needs a multi-N-tile output loop (deferred)' but the actual cause was (a) single-(1,1,1) dispatch and (b) tile_col = gid(0) (global id, not tile index). The spec is right that the idiomatic GPU tiling model is ONE workgroup == ONE output tile, and the grid IS the loop — this is the canonical CUDA/Vulkan/Triton tiling pattern (cf. Triton's pid_m/pid_n from tl.program_id(0/1), which is exactly the GPU-workgroup-id-as-tile-index idiom).

Index math is triple-checked and correct: with @workgroup(32,1,1) and dispatch (N/16, M/16, 1), GlobalInvocationId = workgroup_id * local_size + local_id (SPIR-V spec §Builtin.GlobalInvocationId). gid(0)/32 = workgroup_id.x = tile_col for ALL 32 lanes (since (wx*32+lane)/32 == wx for lane in 0..31). gid(1) = workgroup_id.y = tile_row because local_size.y=1. The asymmetry is correct and necessary.

The division-recovery approach is the ONLY option and already has a GPU-proven precedent in this codebase: matmul_shared_f32.axc uses gid(1)/16 for tile_row and gid(0)/16 for tile_col (AT-1621, GPU-proven bit-exact on Lavapipe + NVIDIA). The coopmat kernel just differs in local_size.x=32 (not 16), hence the divisor is 32 instead of 16.

No new codegen is needed: OpUDiv for u32/u32 is already wired in body.rs (BinOp::Div → em.b.u_div, confirmed in body.rs line 1640); gid(axis) → OpLoad GlobalInvocationId + OpCompositeExtract is wired in emit_gid_component (body.rs lines 1991-2012); subgroup_invocation_id() is already emitted; OpPhi K-loop accumulator is GPU-proven (AT-1707). This is purely a kernel-index + dispatch + test/bench change.

coopmat_store offset c_base = (tile_row*16)*N + (tile_col*16) is already correct: emit_coopmat_store_inline does access_chain [zero, c_base] + OpCooperativeMatrixStoreKHR RowMajorKHR stride N (coopmat.rs lines 234-249). For RowMajor a 16x16 store writes C[c_base + r*N + c] = C[tile_row*16+r, tile_col*16+c]. The formula covers the correct output tile for ANY (tile_row, tile_col).

Bit-exact oracle is sound: integer-valued f16 inputs (A in {1..4}, B in {1..3}, K=32) give per-element sums at most 32*12=384, which is exactly representable in f16 (f16 is exact for integers up to 2048 per IEEE 754 half-precision). Therefore f16 GPU accumulation == f32 CPU reference == integer, and max_diff == 0.0 is achievable and correct to assert.

Non-symmetric M=32,N=48,K=32 fixture (2x3 tile grid, 2 K-blocks for tile_k=16) exercises all distinct (tile_row, tile_col) combinations and makes it impossible to pass by accidental symmetry or single-tile luck. Both tile_k=16 (2 K-blocks) and tile_k=32 (1 K-block) must be bit-exact, which validates the @strategy hole produces correct numerics rather than just structurally different SPIR-V.

Honesty gate is explicit and binding: if the full grid is not max_diff==0 on NVIDIA after the index fix, Coder must stop and report the blocker (coopmat_store offset, staging coverage gap, etc.) rather than relaxing tolerance or shrinking the fixture. This enforces the lesson from the M3.3 wrong-computing situation.

TFLOPS bench design is honest by construction: labels the number as 'effective TFLOPS (honest)', qualifies it as % of datasheet ESTIMATE (not a measured cuBLAS baseline), omits 'competitive' by default, and applies the AT-1582 CpuFenceWall rule (omit % + scheduling-inclusive qualifier). Single-subgroup-per-tile is expected to give a modest TFLOPS — that is documented as the honest deliverable. Multi-warp / register blocking is explicitly deferred.

Lavapipe / CI compatibility is handled cleanly: CoopMatUnsupported typed-skip on AT-1620/1622 (matching the AT-1707 prepare_kernel_checked match pattern already in the test file); matmul_shared_f32.axc (scalar, Lavapipe-runnable) remains untouched as the Lavapipe correctness path (AT-1621).

Regression surface is narrow: only matmul_shared_coopmat.axc (one line change) + dispatch_shared_m32.rs (stub replacement) + new bench file + Cargo.toml entry + DESIGN/ROADMAP prose. AT-1606/AT-1707/AT-1621/AT-1630 test bodies are explicitly marked unchanged.
50GB cap and grid-limit pre-check are carried forward from the existing resident_matmul bench pattern (specified in AT-1710 bench design), satisfying the CLAUDE.md hard rule on memory limits.
concerns: Minor: AT-1720 is described as using the EXISTING spirv-val anchors (at1620_matmul_shared_coopmat_spirv_val_only and at1622_strategy_holes_spirv_val_only). These anchors compile with tile_assignments(16,16,16) and tile_k in {16,32} respectively — both pass spirv-val today. After the one-line tile_col fix the emitted SPIR-V changes only in the OpUDiv constant value (divides by 32 instead of the old gid literal). spirv-val is insensitive to constant values, so the anchors will still pass. This is fine; explicitly note in the anchor test eprintln that the index fix is in the compiled source.

Minor: The bench fixture uses M=N=K=256 by default (256 workgroups dispatched, 16x16 tile grid). With single-subgroup-per-tile the expected throughput is well below peak (each 16x16 tile is computed by exactly 32 lanes, leaving the rest of the SM idle). The bench design acknowledges this explicitly. No concern with the bench design — the concern is only that the printed % of 125 TFLOPS will look low; the design already requires honest labeling, so this is fine.

Minor: The coder_handoff_notes say 'Pass meta.coopmat.as_ref() to prepare_kernel_checked'. Confirm that meta.coopmat is populated for matmul_shared_coopmat.axc (it should be, since coopmat builtins set caps.coopmat = true and that propagates to CompileMeta). This is already the case for AT-1707 (same kernel class), so no issue expected.

Minor: K not a multiple of tile_k is documented as out-of-scope (truncates K-blocks). The fixtures use K=32 and tile_k in {16,32} so this is a non-issue for M3.3b. The precondition should be documented in the kernel header comment as specified.
validation_against_existing: matmul_shared_f32.axc (this repo, AT-1621 GPU-proven): uses tile_col = gid(0)/16, tile_row = gid(1)/16 with @workgroup(16,16,1) and dispatch (N/16,M/16,1). The coopmat variant is the same pattern with divisor 32 (local_size.x=32 instead of 16) and gid(1) already correct (no divide needed, local_size.y=1). The pattern is proven in this codebase.

SPIR-V spec §Builtin.GlobalInvocationId (SPIR-V 1.3, §2.22.1, Khronos): GlobalInvocationId = WorkgroupId * WorkgroupSize + LocalInvocationId. With WorkgroupSize=(32,1,1), GlobalInvocationId.x = WorkgroupId.x*32 + LocalInvocationId.x. Integer division gid(0)/32 recovers WorkgroupId.x exactly (since LocalInvocationId.x < 32). This is the spec-correct derivation for a 1D workgroup tiling.

Triton tiled GEMM (https://triton-lang.org/main/getting-started/tutorials/03-matrix-multiplication.html): pid = tl.program_id(0); num_pid_m/n; pid_m = pid % num_pid_m; pid_n = pid // num_pid_m. AXIOM's approach (one workgroup per tile, tile_col from gid(0)/local_size.x) is the Vulkan equivalent of Triton's program_id-per-tile idiom.

IREE/MLIR linalg-to-spirv lowering (iree-project/iree, iree/compiler/Codegen/SPIRV): maps linalg.matmul to a grid of workgroups via gpu.block_id / gpu.grid_dim, equivalent to Vulkan WorkgroupId. AXIOM derives WorkgroupId.x from GlobalInvocationId.x / WorkgroupSize.x because it does not expose WorkgroupId as a standalone builtin — this is a valid and standard derivation.

Khronos SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix spec (https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Registry/blob/main/extensions/KHR/SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix.asciidoc): OpCooperativeMatrixStoreKHR with RowMajorKHR layout and stride S writes element (r,c) to base_ptr[r*S+c]. With base_ptr at c_base = tile_row*16*N + tile_col*16 and stride=N, element (r,c) lands at C[tile_row*16+r][tile_col*16+c]. The formula is correct per spec.

body.rs line 1640 (this repo): BinOp::Div for ScalarTy::U32 → em.b.u_div(ty_id, None, lhs_id, rhs_id) → OpUDiv. The unit test at body.rs lines 2143-2144 asserts has_op(UDiv) && !has_op(SDiv) for u32 division. This confirms gid(0)/32u32 will compile to OpUDiv without any codegen changes.

emit_coopmat_store_inline (coopmat.rs lines 221-252): access_chain [zero_id, element_offset_id] + OpCooperativeMatrixStoreKHR RowMajorKHR stride_id. element_offset_id is the SPIR-V SSA value produced by evaluating c_base = (tile_row*16)*N+(tile_col*16) in the kernel body. No codegen change needed for multi-tile: the formula is already general.

AT-1707 (this repo, GPU-proven on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000): OpPhi loop-carried coopmat accumulator with K_ITER=4 passes max_diff==0.0. The K-loop structure in matmul_shared_coopmat.axc is the same OpPhi pattern. M3.3b inherits this proof: if AT-1707 passes, the accumulator is correct; the only remaining question for AT-1620 is whether tile_col and the dispatch grid are correct — which is the single-line fix.
external_references: NVIDIA Vulkan cooperative matrix extension (VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix): https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#warp-matrix-functions (analogous CUDA wmma; Vulkan equiv confirmed in Khronos VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix spec)
test_suggestions: The spirv-val anchors (AT-1720 reuse of at1620_..._spirv_val_only and at1622_strategy_holes_spirv_val_only) should add an eprintln noting the tile_col=gid(0)/32 fix is now in the source, so future readers of CI logs can confirm the anchor covers the patched kernel.

Optional (not required for M3.3b): A third AT-1622 tile_k variant could test tile_k=32 with K=64 to give 2 K-blocks for that variant too, making both paths accumulation-load-bearing. The current design (K=32, tile_k=32 → 1 K-block) is valid but a single-block path is trivially correct; 2-block tile_k=32 would be stronger. This is explicitly a suggestion, not a blocker.

The TFLOPS bench should confirm GpuTimestamp availability and gracefully fall back to CpuFenceWall with the scheduling-inclusive qualifier (per AT-1582 rule specified in the design). The design already specifies this; Coder should ensure the timing_source detection and label branching are wired correctly.
AT-1722 (full workspace test + clippy) should be run LAST, after AT-1620/1622 pass on NVIDIA, to confirm no regression to reduction.axc/AT-1606/AT-1707/AT-1621/AT-1630.
summary: The M3.3b design is sound and approvable. The root-cause diagnosis is correct (single workgroup dispatch + raw gid(0) as tile_col), the fix is minimal (one line in the kernel, dispatch grid in the test/bench), the index math is triple-checked against the SPIR-V spec and the existing GPU-proven matmul_shared_f32.axc precedent, no new builtin or codegen is required, the bit-exact oracle is properly calibrated for f16 integer exactness, the honesty gate is binding, and the test matrix (AT-1620/1622 un-stub + AT-1710 bench + AT-1720/1721/1722 regression guards) is complete. The four open questions in the spec are all answered by the design itself. Minor concerns are informational only — none are blockers.
